headline: Trump says he will veto bills but sees room for deal on healthcare
pages: President Donald Trump said Friday he will likely veto many bills that Democrats pass once they take control of Congress next year. He described a pattern in which Democrats send bills, he vetoes them, and after about a month they return with offers, at which point he would say he would veto unless they agree to his terms. Trump called House Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer smart and said he is willing to work with them. He said there is a real possibility of getting a lot done, especially on healthcare, though not exactly what Democrats want, and said immigration is also open to compromise.

Why it matters: it signals how divided government could work in Washington, with effects on programs Idahoans rely on. This national story was reported by the Idaho Capital Sun. Source: Idaho Capital Sun.
